とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.name: Tonkatsu Tonki Meguro Honten
とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.description: A renowned tonkatsu restaurant with a history of nearly 90 years. There is always a line during the day, but turnover is very fast. Their excellent operation is also a must-see: staff ask for your order when you come in, and what you ordered comes out piping hot as soon as you sit down.
とんかつ とんき 目黒本店.reservation: Dinner only, for groups of 4 or more

Nico Chelsea.description: A stylish French bistro tucked away in a back alley of Kagurazaka. It specializes in game meat (gibier). Which game is available depends on that day's supply, but every dish is excellent. You can pick your own wine from the wine cellar, which makes it fun. It is a very popular restaurant, so reservations are essential.

神楽坂 焼鳥 虎.name: Kagurazaka Yakitori Tora
神楽坂 焼鳥 虎.description: A yakitori restaurant on the slightly pricier side for Japan (though still only about $80). The yakitori itself is very good, and the all-you-can-drink plan even includes Yamazaki whisky, so it is great value. It has counter seats only, so going in a small group is recommended. Reservations are essential. Its Tabelog rating is low because it is a new restaurant with few reviews.

純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.name: Suisui Nihonbashi Tokyo
純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.description: A restaurant where you can drink as much as you like from more than 100 kinds of sake collected from all 47 prefectures of Japan. The range of sake is huge, and if you book a course, you can enjoy it all on an all-you-can-drink basis. The food is decent, so this is a place to go for the sake. Reservations for large groups are also possible.
純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店.note: It is unclear how well English is supported.

中国家庭料理大連.name: Dairen (Chinese Home Cooking)
中国家庭料理大連.description: A down-to-earth Chinese restaurant that has long been loved by students and office workers. The pan-fried gyoza are very good. It is definitely not the kind of place that appears in travel magazines, so it is recommended if you want to experience a restaurant where local Japanese people go.

フラクタル.name: Fractale
フラクタル.description: One of the top rum bars in Japan. It is so famous that when it comes to rum in Tokyo, almost every bartender will name this bar. Besides rum, it also has beer and whisky. An authentic bar with a calm atmosphere. Its Tabelog rating is low because it has few reviews; on Tabelog, bars generally tend to get low ratings.

Antonic 中目黒店.name: Antonic Nakameguro
Antonic 中目黒店.description: A small gin bar along the Meguro River. It is a cozy place with only a few counter seats, but you can enjoy gins from all over the world. Gin is also sold in the basement.

ボンディ 神保町本店.name: Bondy Jimbocho Honten
ボンディ 神保町本店.description: One of the most famous curry restaurants in Japan, and the pinnacle of Japanese-style curry. Rather than strong spices, it is known for the richness and mellowness that come from slowly simmering apples and onions. To everyone from South Asia: this is curry adapted to Japanese tastes, so please forgive us (lol).

Shanaiya.description: A restaurant serving yakuzen (medicinal) curry. Despite the name, there is no medicine in it; it is a spice curry made with plenty of ingredients that help with things like recovering from fatigue. Reservations are possible at dinner, but at lunchtime it uses a numbered-ticket waiting system. You can also join the waiting list online, but everyone applies when it opens at 10:30, so you need to be ready at that time.

ラ メゾン ダミ.name: La Maison Dami
ラ メゾン ダミ.description: A small French bistro in Meguro. The food is excellent, and the pâté Reo had here was among the best he has ever eaten in his life.

ホルモンまさる.name: Horumon Masaru
ホルモンまさる.description: A Japanese-style BBQ restaurant. Since you grill offal (organ meat), it may not be very familiar to non-Japanese people, but it is very popular among Japanese people. There is not much regular meat, so it is not really recommended for people who do not like offal.

らーめん 谷瀬家.name: Ramen Taniseya
らーめん 谷瀬家.description: In Japan there is a genre called Yokohama Iekei ramen, based on a pork-bone and soy sauce broth. There are many famous shops in this genre in places such as Yokohama and Shin-Sugita, and this is a well-regarded one that is easy to reach from central Tokyo. There are many Yokohama Iekei shops in Tokyo, but quality varies a lot, so be careful. When you hand over your meal ticket, you can choose the noodle firmness, the strength of the soup and the amount of fat. Reo likes "soft, strong, less fat," but most people generally choose firm noodles.

麺家 黒.name: Menya Kuro
麺家 黒.description: A well-regarded Yokohama Iekei shop in Tokyo. For an explanation of Yokohama Iekei, see the description of Ramen Taniseya.

新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店.name: Shinjuku Yakiniku Gyutan no Lemon (Main Shop)
新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店.description: A shop serving thick-cut beef tongue. Many people may be hesitant to eat beef tongue, but its chewy texture is very popular in Japan. We recommend eating it with rice. There are also sister shops besides this one, so please try whichever is easiest to get to.

バー タロウズ.name: Bar Tarrow's
バー タロウズ.description: An authentic bar in Kagurazaka. It has a very large number of whiskies, and the bartender, who has a wealth of experience and knowledge, serves whisky that suits your taste. We don't know how much English he can speak, but he is a wonderful bartender who, we can say for certain, will serve you attentively while using a translation device or similar. Besides whisky, the cocktails are also delicious, and there is a wide variety of rum and other spirits. You can also smoke cigars.

食酒家 岡宮.name: Shokushuka Okamiya
食酒家 岡宮.description: A traditional Japanese izakaya. It is near the house where Reo used to live, and the seafood is very good. A hidden gem loved by locals.
食酒家 岡宮.note: We think they can hardly handle English, so you will need to use translation tools or similar.

らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店.name: Ramen Benkei (Monzen-Nakacho)
らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店.description: There are two flavors: soy sauce and miso. We recommend soy sauce. It is Japanese junk ramen topped with lots of back fat, and the bowls are quite dirty. But the taste is definitely very addictive. Reo ate so much of this ramen that he gained 5 kg. The main shop is in Asakusa, but he has never been there, so he chose this shop.

とんかつ 丸七.name: Tonkatsu Marushichi
とんかつ 丸七.description: In a traditional katsudon, the fried pork is finished by binding it with egg, but the katsudon here is made by preparing the egg and the fried pork separately and placing them on top of the rice. A popular shop that started the so-called "unbound katsudon" boom in Japan. The tonkatsu is very thick, so it has a huge visual impact and looks great in photos. As for the taste, the sauce is quite sweet and the meat is very thick, so it is quite heavy. Recommended for people who love fried food. The line is very long, so you should be in front of the shop when it opens.

おにぎり ぼんご.name: Onigiri Bongo
おにぎり ぼんご.description: The shop that started an onigiri (rice ball) boom in Japan about five years ago. It was originally a renowned shop known only to those in the know, but its social-media-worthy look went viral and it suddenly became extremely popular. It serves only onigiri and miso soup, and the onigiri packed with fillings and the perfectly cooked rice are very delicious. Honestly, we don't know how popular it is now, but we expect a long line. It seems you can reserve take-out orders, but they seem to accept reservations only by phone, so if you want to make a reservation, please ask Reo.

Age.3 ASAKUSA.description: A fried sandwich shop. Fried sandwiches themselves became popular after we came to the US, so honestly we are in the same position as all of you. It seems they have not only fruit sandwiches but also ones you could eat for lunch. Judging from the photos, they look delicious, crispy on the outside with a rich seasoning inside. We have quite a lot of free time in Asakusa, so why not stop by?

きつねや.name: Kitsuneya
きつねや.description: The gyudon (beef bowl) is simple, but the rich seasoning and the tenderly simmered beef are superb. It opens early in the morning for people who work at the market, but because of that it closes early, at 1 PM, so be careful. Tsukiji is on our schedule, but we may not make it before closing time, so if you want to go here, please let the organizers know.

I’m donut ? Omotesando.description: Japan's first fresh doughnuts with a fluffy texture. They went viral about a year ago, and our impression is that young people flocked to eat them. The texture is said to be completely different from American doughnuts, so if you are interested, please try them. There are several shops besides Omotesando, so look for a shop that fits your plans.

牛カツ もと村.name: Gyukatsu Motomura
牛カツ もと村.description: A shop serving fried beef. In Japan, frying pork or chicken is common, but beef was rare. This shop overturned that convention and succeeded. There are shops not only in Tokyo but also in Osaka and Kyoto, so look for the nearest shop according to your plans.

黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草.name: Kuroge Wagyu Ichinoya Asakusa
黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草.description: Wagyu bowls made with genuine Japanese wagyu. They look very beautiful. It is popular with tourists, but from a Japanese point of view the price is a little too high, so its Tabelog rating is low.

Bar CENTIFOLIA.description: A bar extremely focused on looking good on social media. To put it positively, it is the pinnacle of flair bartending, but honestly it goes so far over the top that it makes you laugh. However, the bartender has won a cocktail competition in Japan, and his skill as a bartender is the real thing. If you look at their social media first and are interested, I think it is a place where you can have a special experience.
Bar CENTIFOLIA.reservation: Yes, but there is a puzzling reservation fee

カラクサカレー.name: Kara-Kusa Curry
カラクサカレー.description: Japanese-style curry. The spices come through, but it is more of a curry where you can taste the natural sweetness of vegetables and other ingredients. The shop has also received a Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand. A small shop with only counter seats. It opened about nine years ago, when Reo was working in Kyoto, and he went there often back then. The service getting more careless every year is a bit of a concern.

スプリングバレーブルワリー 京都.name: Spring Valley Brewery Kyoto
スプリングバレーブルワリー 京都.description: A brewery with an attached craft beer brewing facility. You can compare different beers in a tasting flight. The menu covers a wide range, from Kyoto-style Japanese food to Western food such as pizza and sausages. A lovely place where you can feel the Kyoto atmosphere along with a modern, stylish vibe.

天ぷらすし海鮮米福 四条烏丸店.name: Tempura Sushi Kaisen Komefuku (Shijo Karasuma)
天ぷらすし海鮮米福 四条烏丸店.description: A shop with delicious tempura and seafood. The tempura is not the traditional batter but a crispier, slightly junky style of tempura. Rather than enjoying the tempura on its own with drinks, I personally recommend having it as tendon (tempura rice bowl) for lunch.

キツネ日和.name: Kitsune Biyori
キツネ日和.description: A shop with delicious tofu and fried tofu (aburaage). Going at night is good too, but they also serve breakfast on weekends, so for those who arrive in Kyoto early, I recommend breakfast. It is also close to the hotel. There is a second shop nearby, but that one does not serve breakfast.

よこやまろうそく.name: Yokoyama Rosoku
よこやまろうそく.description: A Japanese izakaya in Pontocho that is particular about its sake. The food is also delicious, and you can eat seafood and Japanese dishes that go well with sake. It is a small shop with only counter seats, so it is better to make a reservation.

酒と炉端 SuSuCoLi.name: Sake to Robata SuSuCoLi
酒と炉端 SuSuCoLi.description: A robatayaki shop (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal). You can fully enjoy the delicious charcoal flavor that only robatayaki can give. Another fun point is that you can drink old-fashioned, nostalgic drinks such as hiyashiame sour and Kyoto akazake bakudan.

炊と酒 SUITO 京都八条口店.name: Sui to Sake SUITO (Kyoto Hachijoguchi)
炊と酒 SUITO 京都八条口店.description: They are particular about their rice, and the takikomi gohan (rice cooked with seasonings and ingredients) is delicious. There are also drinks made with fresh fruit, recommended for people who like drinks that taste like juice.

酒呑気 びんご.name: Sakenonki Bingo
酒呑気 びんご.description: A Japanese izakaya made by renovating an old Kyoto house. All the food is delicious, but among it all the niku-dofu (beef and tofu simmered together) is superb.

窯出し新五兵衛.name: Kamadashi Shingobee
窯出し新五兵衛.description: An Italian restaurant with all-you-can-eat focaccia in five varieties. Its selling point is dishes made in the oven. It is Italian, but it is not a formal restaurant, and you can walk in casually. They also have many drinks other than wine.

いろり焼 晩喰場.name: Iroriyaki Bankuba
いろり焼 晩喰場.description: A robatayaki shop (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal). Another selling point is the live feel of watching the grilling right in front of you.

野菜と魚 en.name: Yasai to Sakana en
野菜と魚 en.description: A shop focused on vegetables and fish. They are particular about their ingredients, and even simple vegetable dishes are very delicious. They also do robatayaki (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal).

お野菜料理と甘味 ISOMATSU(旧:五十松).name: Oyasai Ryori to Kanmi ISOMATSU (formerly Isomatsu)
お野菜料理と甘味 ISOMATSU(旧:五十松).description: The exterior looks just like a Japanese restaurant, but it serves dishes that go well with wine. They are especially particular about vegetables. I think it would be classified as Japanese food, but it skillfully fuses Western techniques. I have not tried them, but apparently they also put effort into sweets.

Sushi Sho in Kyoto.description: An izakaya where you can eat sushi casually. There are many dishes besides sushi, and you can also eat tempura and more. Recommended for people who want to eat sushi but also want other Japanese food.

百圓寿司スタンド えにし.name: Hyakuen Sushi Stand Enishi
百圓寿司スタンド えにし.description: An izakaya where you can drink from noon and eat sushi casually. There are many dishes besides sushi. There are both standing and seated areas, so you can use whichever suits the occasion.

鉄板 フタゴヤ 富小路.name: Teppan Futagoya Tominokoji
鉄板 フタゴヤ 富小路.description: A shop where you can eat yakisoba, grilled offal, Japanese omelet and other dishes made on an iron griddle. There are also dishes not made on the griddle, so you can enjoy a Japanese izakaya menu. Note that there is no okonomiyaki.

遊亀 祇園店.name: Yuki (Gion)
遊亀 祇園店.description: An izakaya run by the Kinkame sake brewery. In addition to many Kinkame sakes, you can enjoy food that goes well with sake. By the way, Kinkame itself is not a famous sake, but it is delicious.

すし酒場 さしす.name: Sushi Sakaba Sashisu
すし酒場 さしす.description: A sushi shop with several locations in Osaka and Kyoto. A popular shop where you can eat delicious sushi casually while standing. There are some booth seats for sitting, but the standing area turns over faster. It is a popular shop that does not take reservations, so unless you go right when it opens, you will have to wait in line for a while.

麺屋 猪一.name: Menya Inoichi
麺屋 猪一.description: A hugely popular shop selected for the Michelin Bib Gourmand nine years in a row. They are very particular about the soup, and it is so full of dashi flavor that apparently some people end up drinking the whole bowl. The shumai side dish is apparently also delicious, so if you have room, you might want to order it. It is a hugely popular shop and apparently hands out numbered tickets, so I recommend going early. There is apparently also a second shop, so if this shop does not work out, you could try the second shop.

やすべえ.name: Yasubee
やすべえ.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop in Pontocho. Besides okonomiyaki, the betayaki, which is a thinly cooked batter topped with cabbage and other ingredients, is apparently also popular.

WAGYU TERIYAKI ITADAKI BURGER Gion Kyoto.description: A wagyu hamburger shop. It does not have a website for Japanese customers and is aimed entirely at overseas tourists. Perhaps because of that, the prices are on the high side for Japan, which I personally don't like, but its Google Maps rating is an astonishing 5.0. Having a 5.0 with more than 3,000 reviews is honestly impressive. The taste is probably the real deal.

麺匠 たか松.name: Mensho Takamatsu
麺匠 たか松.description: The main shop of a ramen chain with locations across Japan. The ramen is delicious too, but I would like to recommend the tsukemen (dipping noodles). The dipping sauce, a chicken base with seafood dashi and more added, is very delicious. They use stone-ground whole wheat noodles, which have a stronger wheat flavor than normal noodles and go down smoothly. Onions and sudachi (a Japanese citrus) are served on a separate plate, so after eating some, you can add these toppings to change the flavor and enjoy it from start to finish. There are several shops, so go to one close to you.

キチ・キチ.name: Kichi Kichi
キチ・キチ.description: A shop famous for omurice (fried rice topped with soft, half-cooked egg). Of course it tastes good, but it is also a dish you can enjoy even before eating because it looks so beautiful. First, please look at the actual omurice on their website or elsewhere. It is reservation only, and you cannot get in without a reservation, so be careful. However, I don't like that they charge $13 just to make a reservation.

麓寿庵.name: Rokujuan
麓寿庵.description: A shop where you can enjoy traditional Japanese tea sweets and tea (matcha, hojicha and more). The hana warabi is truly beautiful, and the shop shows well the character of Japanese sweets, which are also particular about appearance. It seems you can also have meals, but here please be sure to enjoy the Japanese sweets.

み mitarashi-dango.description: A dango shop. They also have traditional-style dango, but what makes this shop popular is its photogenic, beautiful-looking dango. They put sweet bean paste shaped like seasonal flowers on top of the dango. They also have traditional-style dango, but rather than those, please order the beautiful-looking hanamari dango.
み mitarashi-dango.name: Mi mitarashi-dango

祇園辻利 祇園本店.name: Gion Tsujiri (Gion Main Shop)
祇園辻利 祇園本店.description: A matcha shop. One of the most famous matcha shops in Japan. They serve not only matcha for drinking in the original style but also matcha lattes and matcha-flavored sweets. They post a lot of photos on Instagram, but honestly I don't think they are very good. The real thing must be much nicer.

中村藤吉本店.name: Nakamura Tokichi Main Shop
中村藤吉本店.description: A matcha shop. Probably the most popular shop in the Uji area, with the longest lines. They have matcha, but they are famous for parfait-like sweets with matcha ice cream, jelly, shiratama (rice flour dumplings) and more in a traditional Japanese vessel. Even if you go right when it opens, you may wait in line for more than an hour, so please go prepared. There are also shops around Kyoto Station and Gion.

伊藤久右衛門 宇治本店・茶房.name: Itohkyuemon Uji Main Shop and Tea Room
伊藤久右衛門 宇治本店・茶房.description: Along with Nakamura Tokichi Main Shop, a popular matcha shop in the Uji area. The matcha sweets are famous, but you can also eat soba with tea kneaded into the noodles. It is a popular shop, so it is crowded, and please be prepared for a considerable wait. There is also a shop in Gion, so you don't have to go all the way to Uji.

茶寮都路里 祇園本店.name: Saryo Tsujiri (Gion Main Shop)
茶寮都路里 祇園本店.description: A popular matcha shop. There are shops around Kyoto Station and Gion.

京都とんかつ かつ田 四条河原町店.name: Kyoto Tonkatsu Katsuda (Shijo Kawaramachi)
京都とんかつ かつ田 四条河原町店.description: A popular tonkatsu (fried pork) shop. Besides tonkatsu, its fried beef is apparently also famous.

新福菜館 本店.name: Shinpuku Saikan Main Shop
新福菜館 本店.description: A long-established, popular shop famous for its pitch-black soup. The soup, based on chicken bones and pork bones with a strong soy sauce flavor, is addictive. The thin noodles are smooth, go down easily, and are easy to finish. The fried rice, also soy sauce based, is delicious too, so if you have room, I recommend ordering both. There is also a branch in Osaka.

味乃家 本店.name: Ajinoya Main Shop
味乃家 本店.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop. They use more cabbage and a little less batter, but the whole thing is fluffy and light to eat. A popular shop that is also listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. Honestly, okonomiyaki is delicious anywhere, but I thought this one was especially delicious.

うなぎ屋 廣川.name: Unagiya Hirokawa
うなぎ屋 廣川.description: A renowned eel shop in Arashiyama. The unaju, eel grilled over charcoal with a sweet and salty sauce and placed on rice, is exceptionally delicious. As a snack with drinks, there is also unagi shirayaki (eel grilled without sauce), which comes without sauce or rice. Reo likes to share the shirayaki with the people he goes with, have everyone order their own unaju, and share bottled beer among everyone. There is also a shop in the Kawaramachi area. Reservations only, so be careful.

菊乃井 本店.name: Kikunoi Main Restaurant
菊乃井 本店.description: A kaiseki restaurant that has earned three Michelin stars. You can enjoy a Japanese course meal in which each dish is carefully prepared. A place to enjoy a calm meal in a luxurious, Kyoto-style Japanese room. It is a high-end restaurant, so Reo has never been, but it is the kind of place you would want to go to someday. Reservations only.

福太郎 本店.name: Fukutaro Main Shop
福太郎 本店.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop in the Namba area. Listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. Besides okonomiyaki, the negiyaki (green onion pancake) is apparently also delicious. There are also shops in Umeda and other places.

やっこ.name: Yakko
やっこ.description: A kushikatsu shop in the Shinsekai area. Kushikatsu is a dish of vegetables, seafood or meat on skewers, coated in batter and deep-fried. The ingredients here are apparently large and delicious. Dipping a skewer back into the sauce after taking a bite is prohibited, so don't do it.

たこ焼道楽 わなか 千日前 本店.name: Takoyaki Doraku Wanaka (Sennichimae Main Shop)
たこ焼道楽 わなか 千日前 本店.description: A popular takoyaki shop. They have a fluffy texture and are gooey inside, and delicious. Listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. There are shops in various places.

たぶっちゃん.name: Tabutchan
たぶっちゃん.description: A spicy tantanmen shop in the Nipponbashi area. It is open until late at night, so I recommend it as a bowl to finish the night. It is extremely spicy, so people who can't handle spicy food should avoid it.

炉端とおでん 呼炉凪来 京都駅前店.name: Robata to Oden Koronagirai (Kyoto Station)
炉端とおでん 呼炉凪来 京都駅前店.description: An oden shop. Oden is served first as the appetizer, and this oden is all-you-can-eat. Warming up with oden while drinking sake in the cold winter is a classic Japanese winter tradition. Oden is a type of hot pot, and the ingredients are mostly vegetables, fish cakes made from minced seafood, and so on. The ingredients, soaked in a soup full of dashi flavor, are very delicious. There are several shops, so choose one close to your plans.
